value.title: The 30-minute campfire loaf
value.dek: No starter, no oven, no proofing basket. A Dutch oven, a bag of coals and a dough you mix at lunch.
value.body:
Bread is the thing people assume you can't make outside. You can, and it's easier over coals than in most home ovens: a cast-iron Dutch oven is a steam oven with a lid.

Key takeaways

  • Mix at lunch, bake at dusk: four hours does the proofing for you.
  • Two-thirds of the coals go on the lid.
  • Lift the lid once, at 20 minutes.

What you need

Gear for one 900 g loaf
ItemWhy
5.5 qt Dutch ovenHolds steam for the first 15 minutes
18 charcoal briquettesAbout 220°C with 12 on the lid, 6 under
Parchment slingLowers the dough in without burnt knuckles

Count your coals

Two-thirds on the lid, one-third underneath. Bread burns from the bottom first.

Mix at lunch, bake at dusk

Stir 500 g flour, 360 g warm water, 10 g salt and 4 g instant yeast until shaggy. Cover it and forget it for four hours.

Shaping without a counter

Flour the parchment, tip the dough out and fold the four edges into the middle. Flip it seam-down and let it sit while the coals catch.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kc7sqbW3f8Y
⧉ Inline CTA · component

Bake

Lid on for 20 minutes, lid off for 10. Knock the base: hollow means done. A probe should read 96°C.1

Lid on   20 min  ~220°C  12 coals top, 6 under
Lid off  10 min  ~200°C  6 coals under only

Never on a picnic table

A loaded Dutch oven over coals scorches wood. Use the Cable Fold grate or bare ground.

Can I use whole wheat?

Swap up to 150 g. Add 20 g more water, the bran drinks it.

What if it rains?

The lid keeps rain off the dough. Keep the coals under a tarp until you need them.

⧉ Product card · component
  1. At the centre of the loaf, with an instant-read probe pushed in from the side. ↩

value.title: Close several entities at once
value.summary: Group subsidiaries under a parent, run one checklist, and let Ledgerline post intercompany eliminations for you.
value.body:
Multi-entity close lets a parent company close every subsidiary from one checklist. Each entity keeps its own ledger; the checklist and eliminations are shared.

Available on Scale and Enterprise

Multi-entity close needs at least two entities with the same fiscal calendar.

Before you start

  • Every entity has a functional currency set.
  • Intercompany accounts are mapped in Intercompany mapping.

Create a close group

A close group is the parent and the entities it closes. Create one from the dashboard or the API.

⧉ Code tabs · component

Order of operations

StepRuns on
Bank reconciliationEach entity
Intercompany eliminationsThe parent
Consolidated reportsThe parent

Lock periods last

Locking an entity before eliminations post blocks them. Lock the parent after every child.

Troubleshooting

Eliminations didn't post

Check that both sides of the intercompany pair use mapped accounts. Unmapped lines are skipped and listed in the close report.
value.statusNote: Multi-entity close is in beta. The API shape is stable; the dashboard checklist may change before general availability in Q1 2027.

value.title: Why is my bank feed missing transactions?
value.summary: Most gaps are a pending sync or an expired bank login. Reconnect the account and run a 90-day backfill.
value.body:
1. Open Banking › Connections and look for a yellow Reconnect badge.
  2. Click Reconnect and sign in to your bank again.
  3. Choose Backfill 90 days. New lines appear within 15 minutes.

Pending transactions

Banks send pending card charges only once they settle, usually 1–3 business days later.

value.title: Cast-iron skillet cornbread
value.summary: Crisp-edged, barely sweet cornbread baked in a screaming-hot skillet over coals — or in the oven at home.

image.alt: A golden cornbread in a 10-inch cast iron skillet, one wedge cut out
image.name: skillet-cornbread.jpg

items.name: butter
items.prep: melted, plus 1 tbsp for the pan

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.instruction: Set the skillet over medium coals or in a 220°C oven with 1 tbsp butter inside for 10 minutes.

image.alt: Butter foaming in a hot cast iron skillet
image.name: cornbread-pan-heat.jpg

steps.title: Mix
steps.instruction: Whisk the dry ingredients. Stir in the honey, buttermilk, eggs and melted butter until just combined — lumps are fine.

steps.title: Bake
steps.instruction: Pour the batter into the sizzling pan. Cover with the lid and pile coals on top, or bake uncovered in the oven, for 25 minutes.
steps.tip: It's done when a skewer comes out clean and the edges pull away from the pan.

steps.title: Rest
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes in the pan so it slices cleanly. Drizzle with hot honey and flaky salt.

value.notes:
No buttermilk? Stir 1 tbsp lemon juice into 480 ml milk and wait 5 minutes.

Keeps two days wrapped. Reheat wedges cut-side down in a dry skillet.

value.title: Warranty & returns
value.summary: Cast iron and carbon steel are covered for life against cracks, warps and failed welds. Unused items can come back within 60 days for a full refund. Seasoning wear isn't a defect.

clauses.heading: What's covered
clauses.body: Caldera warrants every cast iron and carbon steel product against defects in materials and workmanship, including cracking, warping beyond 1.5 mm and weld failure, for the life of the product.
clauses.plain: If it cracks, warps or a weld fails, we replace it. Forever.

clauses.heading: What isn't
clauses.body: Rust, seasoning loss, discolouration and damage from misuse — including thermal shock from cold water on a hot pan — are not defects.
clauses.plain: Rust and worn seasoning are fixable, not faults. We'll show you how.

clauses.heading: 60-day window
clauses.body: Unused items in original packaging may be returned within 60 days of delivery for a full refund to the original payment method.

clauses.heading: How to start a return
clauses.body: Start a return at caldera.bettercms.site/returns with your order number. We email a prepaid label within one business day.

versions.changes: Returns window extended from 30 to 45 days.
Carbon steel added to the lifetime warranty.

value.title: How Northbeam closes its books in 3 days
value.summary: Northbeam's four-person finance team cut month-end close from 11 days to 3 while revenue doubled — without adding headcount.
value.challenge: Northbeam sells to 6,000 Shopify brands across three currencies. Its finance team reconciled Stripe payouts against bank lines in spreadsheets — 11 days every month, and growing.
value.solution: Ledgerline connected Stripe, two banks and NetSuite in an afternoon. Bank rules matched payouts automatically, and the multi-entity checklist replaced a 140-row spreadsheet.
value.results: Close now takes three days. The controller spends the rest of the month on forecasting instead of matching, and auditors pull evidence straight from the close report.
value.quote: We closed March in three days and nobody stayed late. I didn't think that was possible at our volume.

value.title: Cooking at 3,000 metres
value.summary: Mountain guide Inés Calderón on why water boils at 90°C up high, the one pan she carries up Aconcagua, and dinner for twelve in a snowstorm.
value.showNotes:
Inés guides on Aconcagua and in the Cordillera Blanca. We talk altitude, fuel and feeding a team at the end of a 14-hour day.

Mentioned

  • Carbon Steel Pan 8"
  • One-pot lentils with chorizo
  • Inés's guiding company

chapters.title: Dinner for twelve in a storm

value.transcript:
Mei: Inés, you've cooked on more summits than anyone I know. What surprises people first?

Inés: That pasta never cooks. Water boils at about ninety degrees up there, so everything takes twice as long and you burn twice the fuel.
